Alan Wilson

Republican candidate for Governor and Lieutenant Governor, South Carolina · Open seat

Attorney General of South Carolina (since 2011); attorney; Colonel, JAG Corps, South Carolina Army National Guard

Alan Wilson, a Republican, has been South Carolina's Attorney General since 2011. He announced his run for governor on June 23, 2025. He finished second in the June 9, 2026 Republican primary, then beat Lt. Gov. Pamela Evette in the June 23 runoff to win the nomination. His running mate for lieutenant governor is state Sen. Mike Reichenbach of Florence County.

Where Wilson stands

Education / school choice
Supports universal school choice and calls it a top priority. Says parents should be able to pick the education that best fits their child's needs.
Abortion
Calls himself pro-life. Said he would veto S. 1095, which would remove exceptions for rape, incest and fatal fetal anomalies. Proposes reforming adoption and foster care and funding crisis pregnancy centers.
Medicaid expansion
Opposes Medicaid expansion. Argues that if federal funding is lost, the state could no longer afford teacher pay raises, law enforcement and other services.
Data centers
Opposes a moratorium on new data centers. Supports local control plus state rules requiring approved data centers to generate their own power and setting standards for environmental, noise and light impacts.
Public safety / license plate reader cameras
Says Flock license plate reader cameras can help police in serious cases such as kidnappings and murders. As Attorney General, he has asked Flock for details on how the cameras work and what data they use.
Infrastructure / transportation
Proposes paying for roads without raising taxes. His plan is to reform the Department of Transportation, add toll express lanes built by private companies in highway medians, and keep projects shovel-ready.
Immigration and crime
Makes immigration enforcement and fighting fentanyl trafficking and violent crime central to his public safety platform, and points to his court cases defending immigration enforcement as Attorney General.

Background

  • Attorney General of South Carolina, 2011–present (elected 2010; re-elected 2014, 2018, 2022)
  • Colonel, Judge Advocate General Corps, South Carolina Army National Guard
  • Former assistant solicitor and assistant attorney general; private law practice
  • J.D., University of South Carolina School of Law, 2002
  • B.A., political science, Francis Marion University, 1996
  • Won the 2026 Republican runoff for governor (June 23, 2026)
